title: smock Definition file, format version 1
description: A Definition file declares Mocks, Stubs, or both. smock reads every Definition file of a definitions directory together, as one definition set, so a Stub may belong to a Mock declared in another file. Rules that span the set cannot be expressed in this Schema: Mock names and Stub IDs are unique across the set, every Stub and every Data bucket names a Mock that some file declares, and Data bucket names are unique within their Mock. Nor can the rules of keyed Data buckets, or the names templates read. `smock check <dir>` checks those as well.

version.description: The format version of this file. Version 1 is the only one. A file without version is read as version 1.

stubs.description: The Stubs this file declares, in the order they are tried among Stubs of equal priority (after the Stubs of files whose names come earlier in byte-wise order).

data.description: The Data buckets this file declares: named JSON values of Mocks, each with its initial value. A bucket may sit in any file, apart from its Mock. Templates read a bucket of their Stub's Mock as data.NAME.

mock.description: A Mock: a named set of Stubs that impersonates one dependency service. A request reaches a Mock by its Host.

name.description: The Mock's name, unique across the definition set. Stubs name their Mock by it.

hosts.description: The Hosts this Mock answers to. A request reaches the Mock when its Host is one of them. Hosts are compared case-insensitively, without the port and without a trailing dot, and each one belongs to at most one Mock. Without hosts, the Mock is reached only as the Default Mock.

default.description: Whether this Mock is the Default Mock, which receives the requests whose Host matches no Mock. At most one Mock is marked default. When the definition set declares exactly one Mock, that Mock is the Default Mock without this. Default false.

noMatch.description: How the Mock answers a request that no Stub matches.

status.description: The status of the response when no Stub matches. Default 404.

headers.description: Header fields to send on the response when no Stub matches, such as CORS headers, by name: a value, or a non-empty array of values, each sent as its own field line, in order. They are sent as written, never templated. Names are compared case-insensitively, so two names that differ only in case are rejected. smock sets Content-Type for its JSON body, Smock-Near-Miss, Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding and Connection itself, and Smock-Mock when the Default Mock answers, so they cannot be given. smock sends Date with the current time, unless Date is given here.

not.description: A header field smock sets itself on the response when no Stub matches.

journal.description: Whether the requests this Mock receives are recorded in the Journal. Turn it off so that a high-rate load test pays nothing for recording. Default true (on).

dataBucket.description: A Data bucket: a named JSON value that a Mock declares, with its initial value, inline (json) or in a JSON file (jsonFile). Each Session reads the initial value. The initial value is static JSON, never templated.

mock.description: The name of the Mock the bucket belongs to. One of the Definition files of the set must declare a Mock with this name.

name.description: The bucket's name, unique within its Mock, which templates read as data.NAME: 1 to 128 ASCII letters, digits, _ and -. Two Mocks may use the same name; each has its own bucket.

json.description: The initial value, inline: any JSON value, null included.

jsonFile.description: The initial value, read from a JSON file in UTF-8: a path relative to the body-file subdirectory of the definitions directory (files by default), such as orders.json, with the path rules of bodyFile. It is read when the definitions are loaded, and a file that is not JSON, or that repeats a key in one object, is an error, as for a JSON Definition file.

key.description: Makes the bucket keyed: the name of the member that holds each item's key, taken literally (a.b is the member a.b). A keyed bucket's value is an array of objects. Each has the key member, holding a non-empty string without /, or an integer from -(2^53 - 1) to 2^53 - 1, judged by its 64-bit floating-point value (1.0000000000000001 is the key 1), and no two items have keys with the same text, so 42 and "42" collide. Only a keyed bucket can be served by a CRUD Stub (crud).

newKey.description: How a keyed bucket makes a key for an item that an append adds without one: integer, one more than the highest integer key (string keys are not counted, and an integer whose text a string key has is skipped), or 1 when there is none; or uuid, a version 4 UUID from the request's helpers, which fault.seed repeats. Only a bucket with key takes it. Default integer.

oneOf.description: An initial value from a JSON file.

fileStub.description: A Stub declared in a Definition file: the Stub shape, plus the Stub's ID and the name of its Mock.

id.description: The Stub's ID, unique across the definition set. It names the Stub in the Journal, in metrics and in Near misses.

mock.description: The name of the Mock this Stub belongs to. One of the Definition files of the set must declare a Mock with this name.

stub.description: The shape of a Stub, without its ID and its Mock: the conditions a request must meet, the Scenario state it needs or moves to, the Variables and Data buckets it writes, the response to return (response) or the weighted responses to pick from (responses), and the Faults to inject. A CRUD Stub has crud instead of conditions, a Scenario clause, writes and responses: it serves a keyed Data bucket as a REST resource. A Stub in a Definition file adds id and mock to it (see fileStub). The Admin API adds Ephemeral Stubs in this shape, and gives the Mock and the Session itself. This definition does not close itself to other properties so that those two can extend it; each of them closes it with unevaluatedProperties: false.

priority.description: The Stub's priority: Stubs with a lower number are tried first. A Stub without a priority is tried after every Stub with one. Stubs of equal priority are tried in file-name order (byte-wise), then by their position in the file.

responses.description: Several responses instead of one: a matched request gets one of them, picked at random, each with the probability of its weight over the sum of the weights. 1 to 100 responses, in the order written. The pick draws from the request's one random draw, so fault.seed and --seed replay it, and it leaves the Faults and the template helpers as they would be with response. Give exactly one of response, responses and crud.

variables.description: Variables to write when the Stub matches, by name: each a named JSON value kept per Mock and Session, which templates read as vars.NAME. A name is 1 to 128 ASCII letters, digits, _ and -. A value is any JSON, and is always a structured template, whether or not a response has template: true: ${…} inserts a value, $${ writes ${, and a $if at its root needs else. At the match decision, after the Scenario moves, the values are rendered in the order written against the Variables as they were before the request, then all are written, and the response sees the new values. A value that fails to render writes none of them. Writing null stores null.

dataWrites.description: Writes to the Data buckets of the Stub's Mock, made when the Stub matches: 1 to 100 writes, applied in order. At the match decision, after the Scenario moves, the values of variables are rendered, then the value of each write, all against the state from before the request, Variables included. The writes are then applied in order, and stored together with the Variables, all at once. When a value fails to render, a write cannot be applied (such as a merge into a bucket that holds no object) or the writes would pass the state bound, nothing is written. The response sees the data after the writes, and a Stub with responses writes once, whichever response is picked.

oneOf.description: A CRUD Stub: crud in place of request, response, responses, scenario, variables and dataWrites.

crud.description: What a CRUD Stub serves: a keyed Data bucket of the Stub's Mock, as a REST resource at path. GET path lists the bucket's items that its list query keeps (filters by member, $sort, $offset and $limit), a plain JSON array, with X-Total-Count and X-Filtered-Count; POST path creates an item and answers 201 with it and its Location. GET, PUT, PATCH and DELETE on path/KEY read, replace, update with a shallow merge and delete the item whose key has the text KEY, or answer 404. Reads see the request's Session's copy of the bucket, or else its initial value, and writes go to that Session's copy. Any other method or path shape does not match the Stub, so later Stubs are tried. A CRUD Stub is tried in the usual order, so an earlier Stub can take over one of its requests. Its answers are compact JSON with Content-Type: application/json, never templated, and fault works on it as on any Stub.

bucket.description: The name of the Data bucket served: a bucket of the Stub's Mock that has key.

path.description: The list path, such as /api/v1/orders. An item path is the list path, then /, then one non-empty segment, the key text. Both are compared with the request's percent-decoded path, byte for byte, as path conditions compare it. It starts with /, does not end with /, and has no empty segment, so / alone is not one.

headers.description: Header fields to send on every answer of the Stub, errors included, such as CORS headers, by name: a value, or a non-empty array of values, each sent as its own field line, in order. They are sent as written, never templated. Names are compared case-insensitively, so two names that differ only in case are rejected. smock sets Content-Type, Location, X-Total-Count, X-Filtered-Count, Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding and Connection itself, and Smock-Mock when the Default Mock answers, so they cannot be given. smock sends Date with the current time, unless Date is given here. A browser reads X-Total-Count and X-Filtered-Count only when Access-Control-Expose-Headers names them.

not.description: A header field smock sets itself on the answers of a CRUD Stub.

dataWrite.description: A write to a Data bucket of the Stub's Mock: its op, the bucket, and the members the op takes. set and merge take value and, for a keyed bucket, key; append takes value; remove takes key. On a keyed bucket, merge needs key, and every write keeps the rules of keyed buckets: a write by key to a key that no item has, or one that would break the rules, writes nothing.

oneOf.description: set: the bucket becomes the value, which in a keyed bucket must be an array of objects with valid, unique keys. With key, the item with that key becomes the value, an object, in its place. The value's key member may be absent, and is then added as its last member, or hold the item's key text; the item keeps its stored key value.

merge: a shallow merge of the value, which must be an object, into the bucket, which must hold an object. Each member of the value replaces the member of the same name in its place, or is added at the end; null is stored as null. With key, the merge is into the item with that key, whose key member the value may leave out or give the item's key text. A keyed bucket takes merge only with key.

append: the value is appended to the bucket, which must hold an array. In a keyed bucket, the value is an item, an object: a valid key that no item has is kept, and an item without the key member gets a new key, as the bucket's newKey says, added as its last member.
remove: the item with the key is removed from the keyed bucket.

dataWriteBucket.description: The name of the Data bucket written to, taken literally: one of the buckets of the Stub's Mock, which any file of the set may declare.

dataWriteKey.description: The key of the item written to, in a keyed bucket: a text template, always parsed, whether or not a response has template: true, and compared as a key text, so ${path[3]} finds the item whose key is 1002 or "1002". It renders before the write's value, and is bounded as a rendered body is. Only a keyed bucket takes it.

dataWriteValue.description: The value of the write: any JSON, and always a structured template, whether or not a response has template: true. ${…} inserts a value, $${ writes ${, and a $if at its root needs else. It is rendered against the state from before the request, and bounded as a rendered body is: at most 1 MiB of compact JSON and 10,000 loop iterations. A value with no ${, $each or $if that breaks its op, such as a merge value that is not an object, or a set value without key that breaks the rules of a keyed bucket, is an error when loading.

scenario.description: The Stub's Scenario clause. A Scenario is a named state machine within the Stub's Mock: it has no declaration, exists because Stubs name it, and starts in the state `Started`. Its state is kept per Mock and per Session: requests without a Session share their own. With requires, the Stub matches only while the Scenario is in that state; without it, in every state. With moveTo, the Scenario moves to that state the moment the Stub is chosen, whatever then happens to the response, even a delay, a connection Fault or a template error. Give requires, moveTo or both. Names are compared byte for byte.

name.description: The Scenario's name. Two Mocks may use the same name: each has its own Scenario.

requires.description: The state the Scenario must be in for the Stub to match, such as `Started`. A Stub in another state is skipped, and the next one is tried.

moveTo.description: The state the Scenario moves to when the Stub is chosen. `Started` sends it back to the start.

request.description: The conditions a request must meet for the Stub to match it. Every condition given must hold. An omitted condition matches anything, so a Stub without request matches every request its Mock receives.

method.description: The request method, compared exactly and case-sensitively, such as GET.

path.description: The request path, percent-decoded and without the query: an exact path, or a pattern that must match the whole path.

anyOf.description: An exact path. It starts with /.

query.description: Query parameters, by name, each with a value condition. An exact string or a pattern holds when one of the parameter's percent-decoded values equals the string or matches the pattern as a whole, so it fails when the parameter is absent, and a repeated parameter matches when any of its values does. `$not` and `$exists` are about the parameter as a whole instead, and may hold when it is absent: see valueCondition. Names are literal, even when they start with `$`, such as `$filter`. Parameters that are not listed are ignored.

headers.description: Header fields, by name, each with a value condition. Names are compared case-insensitively. An exact string or a pattern holds when one of the header's values equals the string or matches the pattern as a whole, so it fails when the header is absent, and a repeated header matches when any of its values does. Each header field line is one value: a line that joins values with commas, such as `b, a`, matches only as a whole. `$not` and `$exists` are about the header as a whole instead, and may hold when it is absent: see valueCondition. Headers that are not listed are ignored.

cookies.description: Cookies, by name, from every Cookie header field of the request. Each field is split on `;`, each part is trimmed of spaces and tabs, and the first `=` of a part separates the name from the value; a part without `=` is skipped. Names are compared exactly, case and all, and values exactly as sent: quotes are part of a value, and nothing is percent-decoded. An exact value or a pattern holds when one of the cookie's values equals the given string or matches the given pattern as a whole, so a repeated cookie matches when any of its values does. `$not` and `$exists` are about the cookie as a whole instead, and may hold when it is absent: see valueCondition. Names are literal, even when they start with `$`. Cookies that are not listed are ignored.

body.description: The request body: an exact string, a pattern that must match the whole body, a json condition, a form condition, or an xml condition.

anyOf.description: The exact body, as text in UTF-8.

valueCondition.description: A condition on the values of a name, such as a query parameter: an exact string or a pattern, which one of the values must meet, or an operator about the name as a whole. An object whose only key starts with `$` is an operator; any other `$` key is reserved.

notCondition.description: Negation: the condition holds exactly when the given one does not. So `{"$not": "a"}` holds when no value is `a`, or when the name is absent, and a negated pattern holds when no value matches it. Operators nest.

existsCondition.description: Presence: with true, the name is present, with any value, even empty; with false, it is absent.

pattern.description: A pattern condition, in RE2 syntax. The pattern must match the whole value, not only part of it. Patterns are compiled when the definitions are loaded, and a pattern that does not compile makes the definition set invalid.

jsonCondition.description: A json condition: the body parses as JSON and contains the given value.

json.description: The JSON value the body must contain. An object whose only member is `pattern`, with a string, is a pattern on the value in its place. It matches a string, or the JSON text of a number, `true` or `false`, as a whole; a number's text is its shortest form, so `1.50` is matched as `1.5`. It never matches `null`, an object or an array. Any other object needs each listed key, matched recursively, and may have others. An array needs the same length and is matched element by element. Any other value must be equal. To match an object such as `{"pattern": "a.b"}` itself, nest a pattern in it: `{"pattern": {"pattern": "a\\.b"}}`. An object whose only key starts with `$` is an operator on the value in its place: `$not` holds when the value does not meet the condition it holds, and a missing key holds it when a missing key does not meet that condition, so a missing key meets `{"$not": "x"}` but not `{"$not": {"$exists": false}}`; `$exists` (`true` or `false`) when the value is present, even `null`, or missing; `$includes` when the value is an array with an element that meets the condition it holds; `$last` when the value is an array with at least one element and its last element meets the condition it holds, as in `{"messages": {"$last": {"role": "tool"}}}`. Any other `$` key is reserved, and a key that starts with `$` is written `$$`: `$$ref` is the key `$ref`. smock checks the operators, not this Schema, because literal JSON is valid here.

formCondition.description: A form condition: conditions on the fields of an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body.

form.description: Form fields, by name. They are decoded as query parameters are: `+` and `%20` both stand for a space, and a field without `=` has the empty value. An exact string or a pattern holds when one of the field's values equals the string or matches the pattern as a whole, so it fails when the field is absent, and a repeated field matches when any of its values does. `$not` and `$exists` are about the field as a whole instead, and may hold when it is absent: see valueCondition. The condition holds only when the request's Content-Type is a form's: its media type must be application/x-www-form-urlencoded, compared case-insensitively, with any parameters. Any other Content-Type, or none, fails every listed field, `$not` included, and fails `{}`, which lists no field. An empty body with the form Content-Type has no fields. Names are literal, even when they start with `$`. Fields that are not listed are ignored.

xmlCondition.description: An xml condition: the body parses as XML, and the value at each path meets its condition. The Content-Type is not consulted. A body that is not well-formed XML fails every condition, `$not` included, and fails `{}`, which lists no path; so does a body with a DOCTYPE, in an encoding other than UTF-8, or with elements nested more than 256 deep.

xml.description: Paths into the body, each with a value condition. A path is `/` and element names separated by `/`, optionally ending in `/@` and an attribute name, such as `/Envelope/Body/GetUser/id` or `/order/@status`. Names are local names: a path names no prefix, and prefixes in the body are ignored. A path selects every element it reaches from the root element by child steps, or that attribute of each of them; the condition holds when one of their values meets it, and with none selected only `$not` and `$exists: false` hold. An element's value is all the text in it, CDATA included, trimmed of whitespace. Paths are compiled when the definitions are loaded: `//`, wildcards, predicates, functions and a prefix make the definition set invalid, as does a final `@xmlns`, since `xmlns` names namespace declarations, which are not attributes.

response.description: The response to return when the Stub matches. Its body is given inline (body), read from a body file (bodyFile), given as JSON (json), streamed as Server-Sent Events (events), or declared as an LLM reply (llm). Give at most one of them; without any, the body is empty. With template true, the header values, the body and the events are templates, parsed when the definitions are loaded and rendered for each request: see docs/definition-files.md, Templates.

weightedResponse.description: One of a Stub's responses: a response, as response gives it, with a weight.

weight.description: The response's weight: it is picked with the probability of its weight over the sum of the weights of the Stub's responses, so weights 9 and 1 give it nine requests in ten. Default 1.

responseFields.description: The fields of a response: its status, its headers, its body or LLM reply, and whether it is a template. This definition does not close itself to other properties so that weightedResponse can add weight; response and weightedResponse each close it with unevaluatedProperties: false.

headers.description: Header fields to send, by name: a value, or a non-empty array of values, each sent as its own field line, in order, such as several Set-Cookie fields. Content-Type takes one value. Names are compared case-insensitively, so two names that differ only in case, such as Set-Cookie and set-cookie, are rejected. smock sets Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding and Connection itself, and Smock-Mock when the Default Mock answers, so they cannot be given. smock sends Date with the current time, unless Date is given here.

^[Cc][Oo][Nn][Tt][Ee][Nn][Tt]-[Tt][Yy][P.description: Content-Type takes one value, never an array: smock reads it to escape a templated body.

body.description: The body, inline. It is sent as text in UTF-8.

bodyFile.description: The body, read from a body file: a path relative to the body-file subdirectory of the definitions directory (files by default), such as users/1.json. The path cannot leave that subdirectory, and none of its names start with a dot, since smock skips such files. Body files are read when the definitions are loaded.

json.description: The body as JSON: any JSON value, sent as compact JSON in UTF-8, with Content-Type: application/json unless headers gives a Content-Type. smock writes every number in its shortest form (9.90 is sent as 9.9); use body when the exact bytes matter. With template true, it is a structured template: a string that is exactly one ${expr} gives the value with its own type, an object with $each gives an array, and an object with $if gives its then or else.

template.description: Whether the header values (except Content-Type, which cannot contain ${), the body (body, bodyFile or json) and the events are templates, rendered for each request. With template false, nothing is parsed or rendered: ${ is plain text and $each a plain key. Default false.

events.description: Server-Sent Events to stream instead of a body. smock sends the status and the headers at once, always with Content-Type: text/event-stream (a Content-Type in headers is replaced), then writes each event after its delay, and closes the stream after the last one.

llm.description: An LLM reply, declared by its content instead of a body: smock writes it in the wire form of the API that api names, as a stream of Server-Sent Events with Content-Type: text/event-stream when the request's JSON body has stream: true, and otherwise as one JSON body with Content-Type: application/json (a Content-Type in headers is replaced). smock adds an x-request-id header, unless headers give one of that name in any case; other headers are sent as written. The reply's id and the request id are generated from the Stub's random source, so fault.seed and --seed repeat them; the reply's model is model, or else the request's model when that is a string; its time is when smock received the request. See docs/definition-files.md, LLM responses.

api.description: The LLM API whose wire form the reply takes: openai-chat, OpenAI Chat Completions. It is required and never inferred from the request's path.

text.description: The text of the reply: the content of the assistant's message. Default empty.

id.description: The reply's id, sent exactly as written (smock adds no prefix), in the JSON reply and in every event of the stream. Without it, the id is the API's prefix, such as chatcmpl-, and 24 characters drawn from the Stub's random source. Fixing it changes no other generated id.

model.description: The reply's model, sent as written. Without it, the model is the request's model when that is a string, and otherwise empty. It adds no condition on the request's model: a Stub for one model adds a body condition on it.

usage.description: The token counts the reply reports, as declared: smock counts and estimates nothing. openai-chat gives them as prompt_tokens and completion_tokens, with total_tokens their sum, in the JSON reply, and in a stream only when the request sets stream_options.include_usage to true: then every chunk has usage: null, and a last chunk with no choice gives the usage before [DONE].

input.description: The tokens of the prompt. Default 0.

output.description: The tokens of the reply. Default 0.

stopReason.description: The stop reason, in the word of the API that api names, whatever the reply's content: for openai-chat, the finish_reason stop, length, tool_calls, content_filter or function_call (deprecated). Left out, it is derived: stop.

event.description: One Server-Sent Event. Give exactly one of data and json.

delay.description: How long to wait before writing this event, in milliseconds, counted from the previous event or, for the first event, from the headers. Default 0.

event.description: The event type, sent as the event field. Without it, clients see the type message. One line.

id.description: The event ID, sent as the id field. One line, without NUL characters.

data.description: The event data. Each of its lines is sent as its own data field.

json.description: The event data as JSON: any JSON value, sent as one data field of compact JSON, its numbers in their shortest form. With template true, it is a structured template, as the json of a response is.

fault.description: Faults the Stub injects when it matches. Their random draws come from the Stub's own generator when seed is given, otherwise from the process generator.

seed.description: The seed of the Stub's own pseudo-random generator, so that its random draws repeat on every run. The generator is created when the definitions are loaded and advances once per matched request.

delay.description: A delay before the status line is written, drawn from one distribution: give exactly one of fixed, uniform and lognormal.

uniform.description: A number of milliseconds drawn uniformly from min to max. min must not exceed max.

lognormal.description: A number of milliseconds drawn from a log-normal distribution, for a long tail of slow responses.

sigma.description: The standard deviation of the delay's natural logarithm. The larger it is, the longer the tail.

connectionFault.description: A connection-level Fault, injected instead of the response.

kind.description: reset: reset the connection (RST) without writing anything. close: close the connection without writing anything (FIN). partial: write the status line, the headers and the first half of the body, then close the connection. Each comes once the whole request, body included, has been read, and after the Stub's delay, if one applies. A request that asks for 100 Continue (Expect: 100-continue) gets it before its body is read, and so before any of these.

probability.description: The share of matched requests the Fault applies to, from 0 to 1. Default 1: every matched request.

status.description: An HTTP status code from 200 to 599.

bucketName.description: The name of a Data bucket: 1 to 128 ASCII letters, digits, _ and -.

host.description: A host name or an IP address, optionally with a port, as clients send it in the Host header, such as users.example.com or [::1]:8080. Hosts are exact names: there are no wildcards.

headerName.description: A header field name: an HTTP token.

responseHeaderName.description: A header field name a response can give: an HTTP token, other than a header field smock sets itself.

not.description: A header field smock sets itself.

headerValues.description: A value, or a non-empty array of values, each sent as its own field line, in order.

headerValue.description: A header field value. It contains no control characters other than tab.
